walletSeparation.note: The operator close used a separate shielded wallet key, but the same local test process accessed the owner's Local Devnet DUST secret key to balance and submit fees. This does not prove a deployed operator can execute without any owner wallet key. The valueless owner seed came from the public Local Devnet genesis fixture, not the user's Preprod/development wallet.

publiclyDisclosedForThisSpike: Fixed collateral amount and its shielded-coin Merkle index
Owner, operator, recipient, and position commitments
privateValuesAbsentFromTestedPublicField: Position side, notional, entry price, guard buffer, and salts
Owner close secret and operator close secret

limitations: This is a valueless Local Devnet contract test using two distinct wallets. It is not a Preprod or production transaction.

The operator uses a separate shielded key, but the same local process accesses the owner's Local Devnet DUST secret key for fee balancing and submission. This verifies the caller-key/recipient-key boundary, not a key-isolated production operator or independently funded fees.
The chain runner holds the operator preimage in temporary process memory to exercise both roles. Secure operator-side generation, delivery, and persistence are not verified.
It proves close/claim authority separation and fixed-lot shielded owner readback only; it does not prove oracle pricing, PnL, automated liquidation, safe real-value custody, or a complete perp DEX.
The operator capability has no risk predicate in this spike and can close early at any time.
Only tested raw transaction and indexed contract-action fields were searched for the listed private witnesses; this is not a general privacy audit.
